newsitem.title: USA: SPEED SKATING-SCHENK EARNS TWO MEDALS TO KEEP WORLD CUP LEAD.
newsitem.headline: SPEED SKATING-SCHENK EARNS TWO MEDALS TO KEEP WORLD CUP LEAD.

text.p: China's Ruihong Xue outsprinted Franziska Schenk in a 500 meters race for the second time in as many days, but the German maintained her lead in the in the World Cup speed skating standings.
Xue clocked 39.48 seconds at the distance on the the Pettit National Ice Centre oval to beat Schenk by more than half a second.
But Schenk, who has been bothered by stomach problems the past two weeks, took silver in 40.02 to keep a slim five-point lead over Xue in the World Cup 500 meter standings with 345 points.
Schenk also finished third in the 1,000 meters, retaining her overall World Cup lead in the distance despite passing up Saturday's 1,000 because of illness.
Local favourite Christine Witty won the 1,000 meters in 1:20.42, slower than Saturday's 1:20.19 but good enough for her second gold medal of the weekend.
Witty's two victories moved her into second place in the 1,000 standings with 301 points, 29 behind Schenk.
"I think I'll just get stronger from here on out," predicted Witty.
Sabine Volker of Germany finished second Sunday with a time of 1:20.78.
Japan's Manabu Horii retained his lead in the men's standings over both distances with a victory in the 1,000 and a second place in the 500.
Horii clocked 1:12.76 to claim 1,000 meters gold. He increased his lead over Casey Fitzrandolph by 303 to 271 after the American finished second in 1:12.93.
Russia's Sergei Klevshenya won the 500 in 36.49 seconds, a mere three hundredths of a second faster than Horii. But the Russian still trails Horii by 100 points in the 500 meter standings.
